guides.favoredWhen: He solves range with W-W-R gap-close and Edge of Night second for E. Punish wasted E, push and roam if he turtles.

keyTips.text: A good VelKoz never lets him close: use W-W-R to reach.
Edge of Night second blocks his E, then kill.
A wasted E is the window: go when it misses.

early-lane.text: Zed often places Living Shadow before Death Mark so he can swap away from skillshots. Hold your crowd control until he has used the swap.

win-condition.text: Death Mark always lands Zed behind his target. Pre-aim crowd control and escapes behind you, not toward where he cast it.

tips.text: His long-range poke: stay healthy, never trade chunked.
If he turtles under tower, shove and roam.
Death Mark always lands Zed behind his target. Pre-aim crowd control and escapes behind you, not toward where he cast it.
Block then close: EoN eats E, W-W-R finishes.
E down plus item online: the VelKoz who never misses E never wins.

keyTips.text: Use Plasma Fission poke to make the opponent respect the range; wave pressure with Plasma Fission and Void Rift can also give room to help with objectives.
Before level six, keep the wave nearer your side because Vel'Koz is fragile and lacks a reliable escape.
Save Tectonic Disruption as the only self-peel rather than spending it casually; a blink or ranged crowd control can punish it being down.

tips.text: Do not push up until the position of the enemy jungler is known; his immobility makes ganks dangerous.
Life Form Disintegration Ray roots Vel'Koz in place, so channel from a safe angle where ranged crowd control cannot interrupt it.
At level six, the ultimate completes his kit and makes clumped fights more dangerous for the enemy.
The first item component lets Void Rift clear waves more often, helping prevent the opposing mid from roaming freely.
Trade Plasma Fission from maximum range and return to the wave immediately instead of lingering in range of gap closers.
When allies rotate into mid after taking their lane tower, move to a side lane to keep collecting farm and experience.
Clear before sieging or defending a siege, then look for a favorable trade while landing poke.
Around Dragon or Baron, use abilities to catch someone out of position; convert a kill into the objective.
Two ultimate points at level eleven improve follow-up damage, especially when fights are clumped near an objective.
The passive can stack across several enemies in close fights, so chokepoints are useful places to contest.
Stay with the team late rather than splitting; an isolated Vel'Koz can be picked before a fight.
Look for isolated targets, then collapse with allies to win the numbers advantage.
Poke before committing to a fight and keep checking positioning so the attempt to harass does not get punished.
Use chokepoints to make multi-target ability hits and passive procs more likely.

itemization.text: Take Arcane Comet, Manaflow Band, Transcendence, and Scorch with Cut Down and Legend: Haste as the 16.21 rune page.
Build the popular path of Luden's Echo, Sorcerer's Shoes, Shadowflame, Zhonya's Hourglass, and Rabadon's Deathcap.
Start Doran's Ring, a Health Potion, and Stealth Ward.
Choose Horizon Focus as the fourth-item replacement for Zhonya's when wanting more long-range damage or facing immobilized targets.
Max Q, then W, then E, taking Life Form Disintegration Ray at levels six, eleven, and sixteen.

keyTips.text: Harass with Plasma Fission and Void Rift; the Void Rift slow helps set up Plasma Fission and Tectonic Disruption, while the stun can punish a target that steps out of position.
Keep Tectonic Disruption for peel when the enemy can engage; spending the only self-peel carelessly leaves the immobile support open to an all-in.
At level six, use Life Form Disintegration Ray to finish or pressure grouped enemies; first poke them down and channel from a safe position because crowd control can interrupt it.

tips.text: After the bot outer tower falls, rotate mid, pressure the tower, and poke the defender away from the objective.
Use the Void Rift slow to help allies land their crowd control when a direct kill is not available.
Hold the stun for an approaching diver rather than throwing it into the wave when the enemy pair is healthy.
Delay a full fight while Plasma Fission poke lowers the enemy team, then commit when targets are softened.
Check the next major objective and establish vision early from a safe route, then retreat to the team.
Do not cross the map or ward alone; the support is easy to catch without allies nearby.
Level nine maxes Plasma Fission for long-range poke; level eleven adds an ultimate point for finishing low targets.
At level thirteen, Void Rift reaches max rank and adds more damage to the Plasma Fission follow-up.
Ward major objectives and high-traffic paths late so the team can see the enemy approach.
Stay with allies and avoid solo warding unless the enemy position is known; getting picked creates a four-versus-five.
Use Tectonic Disruption to peel and protect the carries through the fight rather than trying to stand in front.
Use fog and range to poke or finish squishies, but keep enough safety to complete the ultimate channel.

itemization.text: Take Arcane Comet, Manaflow Band, Transcendence, and Scorch with Cheap Shot and Ultimate Hunter as the 16.21 rune setup.
Build the popular path of Zaz'Zak's Realmspike, Sorcerer's Shoes, Luden's Echo, Shadowflame, and Zhonya's Hourglass, followed by Rabadon's Deathcap.
Start with Health Potion, Amplifying Tome, and Stealth Ward as early purchases.
Choose Liandry's Torment to replace Shadowflame in the fourth slot when the enemy team has several tanks.
Max Q, then W, then E, taking Life Form Disintegration Ray at levels six, eleven, and sixteen.
